summary: 1955 steel tower near Richardsville, Culpeper County, Virginia, replacing a c.1935 wooden tower; privately owned, listed standing, location withheld.

access.note: Privately owned; the Register says coordinates are unlisted at the owner's request.

events.note: Built by a crew of 12 (Register: foresters and game wardens; newspaper: chief forest wardens or foresters)
Replaced a wooden tower of the same height built by the Civilian Conservation Corps about 1935
Richardsville station manned for the past five years during the fire season by Milton Brooks, per the 1955 report

corrections.why: The Register lists a private owner as administrator and says coordinates are unlisted at the owner's request.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Register says 12 foresters and game wardens built the tower; the 1955 newspaper says 12 men whose jobs were chief forest wardens or foresters. The story reports both.

notes_for_editor: Standing status rests on the Forest Fire Lookout Association list; the Register does not say standing in words. Staffing 'seasonal' comes from the 1955 newspaper about the Richardsville station, presumed to be this tower's site; no later staffing source. Brief's access 'unknown' corrected to private. A 2019 Facebook group post (Abandoned in Virginia) mentions an old fire tower on the Richardsville road; social media, not used. Coordinates withheld by owner; do not publish a location. No photos added; the Register credits a photo to Kristin Reynolds but no image URL was read. Not verified: condition, current owner's name, any closure or public access.
